The smallest such N is 34, with m = 66.

Suppose one person writes m and wins. Then m = (2/3)·(S/N), where S is the total of all N numbers, so S = 3Nm/2. The other N−1 people must then write numbers summing to

S − m = m(3N−2)/2.

Each of those numbers is an integer between 0 and 100, so the sum must be an integer and at most 100(N−1). Any such integer sum in [0, 100(N−1)] can be reached, so the condition is

m(3N−2)/2 ≤ 100(N−1), which gives m ≤ 200(N−1)/(3N−2) < 200/3 ≈ 66.67.

Hence m ≤ 66 for every N.

Now check m = 66. The others must sum to 33(3N−2) = 99N − 66, and this must be at most 100N − 100. That gives N ≥ 34.

For N = 34, the others sum to 99·34 − 66 = 3300 = 100·33, so all 33 others write 100. The total is 3366 and the average is 3366/34 = 99. Two-thirds of 99 is 66, so the person writing 66 wins.

Therefore m = 66 and the smallest N is 34.

ANSWER: 34
